resolutions.resolution: RE-EXPRESSED WITH THE RULING NAMED (D-51), in the scenario recognizer — the extra premise IS the derived answer. FALSIFIED IN ISOLATION, and the two reviewers' attribution does not agree with the measurement: (a) dropping the `this.membershipParent(command, occurrence.parent?.command)` argument at execution.ts:455 leaves the cell RED (`1 failed | 41 skipped`) and leaves the statement stream unchanged — same premise at the same position, same `[MATCH rows=1]` — so contracts finding 2's claim that `membershipParent` is a second sufficient cause for THIS cell does not reproduce; (b) replacing `correlationParent`'s body with the base answer (`verb === "update" && edge.kind !== "junction" ? parent.fields : parent.located!.fields`) turns the cell green but turns three N5 pin cells red (`published-key.test.ts` > `a child-held arm placed after the parent's write names the key that write published`, both routes, and `correlated-membership.test.ts` > `locates and writes the row the parent's own SET ends on`), so reverting is not available. DERIVATION: seed 7160 is rootCount 1 / compound-omitted / `upsert-missing` with `serial: { increment: 100 }`; the arm is placed AFTER the parent's write and its lookup names the parent by the key that write published, so the read genuinely depends on an earlier write of this operation — N1/D-51 — and on the batch route the found requirement rides that batch as a premise over the SAME selector (`Selection.outsideMembership`, gated by `premised = requirement && usesBatch && lookup.dependent`, machinery that predates N5). A temporary instrumentation of `afterStatement` (applied and restored from a backup copy) shows the full stream: the premise (`__viborm_assert__`, 1 row) and THEN the real choice locate over `cs03_a_children` returning 0 rows, followed by the missing arm's INSERT. So no cut was lost and no statement is wrong; the recognizer read the WHERE only, matched the premise first, and read the engine's assert row — which is always exactly one row. The lookup is NOT wrongly marked dependent, and the premise cannot be narrowed without weakening the found requirement.

resolutions.pin: tests/raptor3/g4/parity/published-key.test.ts > `a correlated arm that took its MISSING arm moved nothing, so the row is still at the key it was located by` — NEW, both routes (live and batch-only). HOW THE CELL REACHES THE SHAPE: the shared primary key is the only edge where a membership naming no target is both writable and observable (`accountId` is the card's identity AND its foreign key, so re-addressing the observation moves the record's own WHERE off the row, which a non-identity FK such as `piece.ownerId` would not show). The reference must not be enforced, so the cell SUPPLIES its own `better-sqlite3` database with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` through the existing `SQLite3DriverOptions.client` seam (`world(options?)` / `make(options?)`, a 3-line widening), which is what a provider without foreign keys — PlanetScale — or a schema pushed without them gives. It then creates `card { accountId: 'ghost' }`, runs `card.update({ where: { accountId: 'ghost' }, data: { account: { upsert: { create: { id: 'fresh', ... }, update: { id: 'moved' } } } }, select: { accountId: true } })` and pins `{ accountId: 'fresh' }`, the card row moved to `fresh`, and exactly one new account.

resolutions.finding: M4 (major, commands finding 4) — `exclusiveMemberMove` is raised from `captureSeries`, which on the batch route runs behind the enclosing parent's own already-committed segment, so the three sentences claiming the refusal is `ahead of every write` / `before anything is queued` (execution.ts:1106, AGENTS.md:1084, note.md §1 wave 2a) are false, and no cell measures a parent that writes.
resolutions.resolution: NARROWED CLAIM (no mechanism change) + NEW CELL. DERIVATION of the `if not` branch: the refusal's fact is the captured COUNT, which only the capture can produce, so the refusal cannot be stated earlier than the capture. The capture cannot be moved ahead of the parent's own statement: it reads the members by the parent's membership value, and when the parent's write moves that key the cascade must have happened before the members are captured — that is exactly the N5 published-key fact (`published-key.test.ts`, `a before-child's transition publishes the key ... its later children ... all name`), and `execution.ts`'s own measured comment plus `tests/raptor3/post-prep/g29-dependency-boundaries.test.ts` record that moving captures is what was tried and rejected (`Sibling ORDER is restored where it was actually inverted — by compiling a set mutation as one statement instead of a capture — not by moving the captures that remain`). Even placed ahead of the parent's own statement the claim would still be false, because a `before` child's write is queued earlier still. So the honest fact is stated instead: the refusal is stated where the observed count is FIRST KNOWN; a capture flushes and on the batch route a flush commits what is queued before it, so an enclosing parent's own segment is durable when the refusal fires. The two routes keep ONE result — the same registered sentence, and neither writes anything of the member it names — and differ only in what stands committed behind it, which is D-51's succession.

resolutions.finding: T1 (major, transport finding 1) — executeMember's `holdsWrite` gate suppresses the boundary a later member's observation needs; shapes (A) board.create and (B) board.update+scalar raise UniqueConstraintError on N5, ok at 96ae14d7f
resolutions.resolution: Repaired at one owner (OperationContext). The rule now stated once: a member takes a boundary exactly where a LATER member must OBSERVE an earlier member's effect, and it is the OBSERVING member that takes it. `answer()` — the one place this operation reads from outside its own queue — dispatches first when `TransportAttempt.holdsOtherMemberWrite(this.executingMember)` says some other record of the series left a write waiting. The enclosing write's pendency no longer decides whether the series gets to see itself: it only DEFERS the boundary `executeMember` would take at a member's end (that packaging arm is unchanged). A read taken outside every member claims nothing, because an ordered observation (N1) is stated INSIDE the queued unit on purpose. Two alternatives were falsified and the falsifications are recorded in the doc comment: (a) taking no member boundary at all collapses the per-member packaging that `post-prep/g29-member-dependency` + `g29-dependency-choices` pin (10 cells red); (b) claiming the boundary at EVERY read (not just a member's) splits the unit an ordered observation is stated inside — `g4/parity/ordered-observation.test.ts` "nothing of the unit commits" + `lax-to-one.test.ts` (8 cells red). The discriminator was measured, not guessed: instrumenting the claim site showed the needed shape reads with `executingMember` set while another record's writes wait, and the must-not-claim shapes read with no member executing at all. The createMany-rollback fact is preserved by construction: a series whose members only write reaches no observation. `tests/raptor3/g3/generation/generated-transport-smoke.test.ts` and `node scripts/run-raptor3.mjs g3-transaction-array` both re-checked and gate-verified.

resolutions.finding: C2 (major, contracts finding 2) — the parent premise declared at the INSERT turns g2-transport.test.ts red: an ordinary UPDATE publishes recordSeriesProgress where the contract pins none / pins phase 'member'
resolutions.resolution: Repaired entirely at my owner; NO hunk is needed in `membershipParent` or anywhere else in the other owner's files. The derived answer is the one the brief states: a premise is not a record series member. Two gates asked "are there continuations?" when they meant "has this operation a committed prefix of its own writes?". (i) `run()`'s catch: a generated-output continuation is only ever pushed AFTER the `submit(true, member)` that published the identity it re-pins, and that submit drained a member, so `committedSegments > 0` already holds whenever such a continuation exists — the `continuationCount ||` disjunct was redundant for it and was firing only for the membership premise, which is declared AHEAD of every segment. It is deleted: one decision fewer. (ii) `submit()`'s throw: it now asks `continuations.length > 0` — the guards THIS dispatch carried — instead of `continuationCount`. A guard rides only a segment after the one that wrote what it re-pins, so its presence IS the committed prefix; a continuation still `declaring` carries no guard and says nothing. `continuationCount` survives only where it is still the right question: the `lone`-statement gate, where any guard (either kind) means the batch is not one statement.
